newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling strengthens in subdued market.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling strengthens in subdued market.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling firmed marginally against the dollar on Wednesday in rangebound trade, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 53.47 against the dollar from 53.49 on Tuesday while against the pound, it was posted at an average of 87.30 from 87.45.
"The shilling is steady," one dealer said.
Dealers said that the shilling was trading within a narrow band of 53.35/55 and appeared well-matched against the dollar.
But some dealers added that they were still positioned for a further appreciation of the shilling, albeit marginal, sometime before the end of the week.
"Some corporates replenish their Kenya shilling accounts at the end of the month so we're expecting some dollar inflows," one dealer said.
The money market tighter on an outflow of funds to the secondary market. Overnight rates were quoted at between 14-15 percent from 8-10 percent.
